2026-08-06T12:58:42.4610191Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4610563Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4610881Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4611352Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4611748Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4612970Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4614580Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4616291Z >
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4619318Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4621856Z >
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4622646Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4624039Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4624229Z ### How to Use
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4624458Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4625243Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4625968Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4626136Z ```bash
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4626686Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4627417Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4628021Z ```
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4628219Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4628480Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4631916Z ```bash
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4632484Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4633283Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4634117Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4634839Z ```
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4635038Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4635681Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4637605Z ```bash
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4639044Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4639943Z ```
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4640967Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4641387Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4642231Z ```bash
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4642755Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4643621Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4644610Z ```
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4645154Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4645592Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4646184Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4647597Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4649782Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4649980Z ```bash
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4650475Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4652534Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4653541Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4653866Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4654363Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4655353Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4656148Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4656624Z ```
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4656822Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4657556Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4658707Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4659060Z ```bash
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4659944Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4660824Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4661524Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4661948Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4662338Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4663135Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4663671Z ```
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4663874Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4664298Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4666087Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4667070Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4668021Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4669004Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4670277Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4671090Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4671478Z ### Notes
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4672079Z 
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4672693Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4674082Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4675309Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4676535Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4678172Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4679543Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4680511Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-06T12:58:42.4681211Z </mcp-clis>
